descriptionChirho: The basic Qal meaning of שָׁלַח: to send a person, messenger, or thing to a destination; Arabic أَرْسَلَ (arsala), Korean 보내다, Swahili kutuma, Hindi भेजा — covering all Qal inflections (perfect, imperfect, imperative, infinitive, participle, cohortative) with the core 'dispatch/send' semantics.

The Qal sense of שָׁלַח meaning to stretch out or extend (especially the hand); Arabic مَدَّ (madda), Korean 내밀다/뻗다, Swahili kunyoosha, Hindi बढ़ाया — semantically distinct from 'send' and consistently rendered with 'extend/stretch' equivalents across translations.

The Piel intensive of שָׁלַח with the core meaning 'send/dispatch' — sending messages, messengers, or delegations with purposeful intent; Arabic أَرْسَلَ (arsala), Korean 보내다, Swahili kutuma, Hindi भेजा — all Piel inflections where the meaning is active dispatching rather than releasing or dismissing.

The Piel of שָׁלַח meaning to send away, dismiss, let go, or release — often of divorcing a wife, freeing slaves, or dismissing persons; Arabic أَطْلَقَ (atlaqa) / صَرَفَ (sarafa), Korean 보내다 with 'away' markers, Swahili kuachia/kuruhusu, Hindi छोड़ दिया/विदा किया.

labelChirho: to send out, expel, drive out (Piel)
descriptionChirho: The Piel of שָׁלַח meaning to expel, drive out, or cast out — a more forceful sense than mere dismissal; Arabic أَخْرَجَ (akhraja) / طَرَدَ (tarada), Korean 내보내다, Swahili kutoa/kufukuza, Hindi निकाला — used of expulsion from a place.

labelChirho: to set fire, send fire upon (Piel)
descriptionChirho: The Piel of שָׁלַח in the idiom of sending fire, i.e. setting fire to or burning — a distinct metaphorical extension; Arabic أَشْعَلوا (ash'alu), Korean 불태웠다/불살랐다, Swahili wakateketeza, Hindi जला दिया.

Passive voice of שָׁלַח — being sent or dispatched, or being let loose/released; Arabic مُرْسَلٌ (mursalun), Korean 보내지다, Swahili kutumwa, Hindi भेजा गया — covering Qal passive participle and Pual forms.
